proofs.proof_tex:
On the stated Gaussian variance-reset subclass, equation (22), as recorded in \(\mathrm{def{:}source\mbox{-}margins}\), gives
\[
 \lambda_i(R(M))\in\{0\}\cup[g_0,\infty)
 \quad\text{for every }M\subseteq[n]\text{ and every }i\in[n].
 \tag{11}
\]
In particular (11) holds for every matrix occurrence reached by \(\mathsf A\), so it is the reached eigen band.  The separately stated condition \(c_{t,j}(P)\in\{0\}\cup[h_0,1]\) is exactly the reached projector band.  The Gaussian structural, intervention, mixing, conditioning, and sampling conditions in the theorem are the remaining member properties of \(\mathrm{def{:}promised\mbox{-}class}\).  Hence
\[
 P\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa).
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}promised\mbox{-}transcript\mbox{-}certificate}\) now supplies the recover-or-abstain guarantee, the exact environment-labelled transitive closure on return, and the stated encoder error bar.  This implication uses the Gaussian covariance model and therefore proves no upward transfer of the positive certificate to the source's larger smooth soft-intervention class.

For the family comparison, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}separation\mbox{-}family}\) proves for every \(n\ge4\) that
\[
 \mathfrak F_n\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(1/40,1/2,32),
 \qquad
 0<\eta^{\ast}(P)\le2^{-2n-1}.
 \tag{12}
\]
It also proves directly that \(\mathfrak F_n\) has smooth positive causal conditionals, one legal distinct single-target intervention per node, the parent-ratio property in Assumption 1, and the required score consistency.  It is therefore a member of the published model class, not merely of a newly constructed analogue.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}promised\mbox{-}transcript\mbox{-}certificate}\) recovers on this family under constant public gaps \(g_0=1/40\) and \(h_0=1/2\).

Let \(c>0\) be arbitrary.  Because \(2^{-2n-1}\to0\), choose an integer \(n_c\ge4\) such that \(2^{-2n_c-1}<c\).  Applying (12) at \(n_c\) gives a legal, recoverable published-class member with
\[
 0<\eta^{\ast}(P)<c.
\]
Since this holds for every \(c>0\), no positive constant independent of dimension can be a necessary lower bound on the all-subset margin for recovery.  This is the exact quantifier justified by the family.  It does not say that the margin vanishes at a fixed \(n\), and it does not refute the source theorem's existential premise: by (12), the interval \((0,\eta^{\ast}(P))\) is nonempty for every fixed member.

Nevertheless, any threshold satisfying that premise on \(\mathfrak F_n\) must obey
\[
 0<\eta<\eta^{\ast}(P)\le2^{-2n-1},
 \qquad\text{so}\qquad
 \eta^{-1}>2^{2n+1}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Thus the equation-(22)-controlled sufficient analysis operates at an exponentially small resolution scale on this family.  Its displayed sample requirement has positive inverse-power dependence on that threshold, so (13) makes that sufficient sample bound exponential in \(n\), while the present Gaussian certificate uses the constant reached gaps \(1/40\) and \(1/2\).  This proves exponential pessimism of the sufficient bound on the family without asserting failure of its existential hypothesis.

The projector qualification is algebraic.  Since \(H=G^{\dagger}\), biorthogonality gives \(H_{i,:}G_{:,i}=1\), and Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\ge1.
\]
Every product of orthogonal projectors has operator norm at most one, so the norm product cannot be the asserted general projector-product value when it is strictly larger than one.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}projector\mbox{-}geometry}\) instead proves the valid reciprocal lower bound \(\rho_i(G)\) for any witnessed nonzero comparison.  No step above uses the false printed identity.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/4\), all three densities defining \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{log}}\) are normalized, strictly positive, and smooth.  They admit an acyclic structural realization with the two stated distinct legal single-target interventions and observational graph \(\mathcal G_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{log}}\); consequently, \(\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G_{0}^{\mathrm{log}})\) is empty, whereas \(\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{log}})\) contains \(1\to2\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).  For \(\varepsilon>0\), the intervention likelihood ratio at node \(2\) depends nontrivially on its parent, so the parent-ratio requirement in Acartürk et al.'s Assumption 1 holds; the corresponding root condition is vacuous.  There is a constant \(C<\infty\), independent of \(\varepsilon\) and the environment, such that
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{log}}\subseteq
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{src}}(K_{\mathrm{Leg}},C).
\]
Finally, for every integer \(N\ge1\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(
   \bigotimes_{e=0}^2(P_{\varepsilon}^{[e]})^{\otimes N},
   \bigotimes_{e=0}^2(P_{0}^{[e]})^{\otimes N}
 \right)
 \le \frac{N\varepsilon}{4}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{as }\varepsilon\downarrow0.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The change of variables \(u=\tanh(z_1/2)\) gives
\[
 \frac{du}{dz_1}=\frac{1-u^2}{2},
 \qquad
 \ell(z_1)=\frac{1-u^2}{4},
 \qquad
 \ell(z_1)\,dz_1=\frac12\,du,
\]
and the analogous identities hold for \(v\).  Hence, under \(\mu\), the variables \(U\) and \(V\) are independent and uniform on \((-1,1)\).  Their means are zero.  It follows successively that
\[
 \int w_{\varepsilon,0}\,d\mu=1,
 \qquad
 \int w_{\varepsilon,2}\,d\mu=1,
\]
and, conditioning first on \(U\),
\[
 \int w_{\varepsilon,1}\,d\mu
 =\mathbb E\!\left[(1+aU)\mathbb E[1+\varepsilon UV\mid U]\right]
 =\mathbb E[1+aU]=1.
\]
Because \(|U|,|V|<1\), \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/4\), and \(a=1/4\),
\[
 w_{\varepsilon,0}\ge\frac34,
 \qquad
 w_{\varepsilon,2}\ge\frac34,
 \qquad
 w_{\varepsilon,1}\ge\frac9{16}.
\]
Thus every density is normalized and strictly positive.  Smoothness follows because \(\ell\), \(\tanh\), and the displayed products are smooth.

The observational marginal of \(Z_1\) is \(\ell(z_1)\), since integration over \(v\) removes \(\varepsilon uv\), and its conditional density for \(Z_2\) is
\[
 p_{\varepsilon}(z_2\mid z_1)=\ell(z_2)(1+\varepsilon uv).
 \tag{1}
\]
Use independent uniform noises and the inverse conditional distribution functions of the positive densities to generate first \(Z_1\) and then \(Z_2\) from (1).  This is an acyclic structural realization.  At \(\varepsilon=0\), (1) is independent of \(z_1\), so its minimal observational DAG is empty.  If \(\varepsilon>0\), then
\[
 \partial_{z_1}\log p_{\varepsilon}(z_2\mid z_1)
 =\frac{\varepsilon u'v}{1+\varepsilon uv},
 \qquad u'=\frac{1-u^2}{2},
\]
is not identically zero.  Thus the conditional mechanism genuinely depends on node \(1\), and the minimal DAG contains precisely \(1\to2\).  Replacing the root density by \(\ell(z_1)(1+au)\) leaves (1) unchanged and gives density \(w_{\varepsilon,1}\).  Replacing the second conditional by \(\ell(z_2)(1+av)\) leaves the root law unchanged and gives density \(w_{\varepsilon,2}\).  Both replacements differ from the corresponding observational mechanism, so they are distinct legal single-target interventions.

For the second intervention, the intervention-to-observation conditional likelihood ratio is
\[
 r_{2,\varepsilon}(z_1,z_2)
 =\frac{1+av}{1+\varepsilon uv}.
\]
When \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \partial_{z_1}r_{2,\varepsilon}
 =-\frac{\varepsilon u'v(1+av)}{(1+\varepsilon uv)^2}
 \not\equiv0.
\]
Thus the ratio depends nontrivially on the sole parent.  This is exactly the parent-ratio requirement for node \(2\); node \(1\) has no parents, so its parent requirement is vacuous.

We next verify one common bounded kernel and the source representation.  Expanding the integrand and evaluating its even cosine moments gives the Laplace representation
\[
 P_j(x)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\pi
 \bigl(x+i\sqrt{1-x^2}\cos\theta\bigr)^j\,d\theta,
 \qquad -1\le x\le1.
\]
The integrand has modulus at most one, so \(\|P_j\|_\infty\le1\), with equality at \(x=1\).  Differentiating the three-term recurrence and inducting gives
\[
 P_j'(x)=\mathop{\sum_{0\le k<j}}_{j-k\,\mathrm{odd}}(2k+1)P_k(x),
\]
whose coefficients sum to \(j(j+1)/2\).  Rodrigues' formula and integration by parts give orthogonality, its normalization, and the Legendre differential equation.  Consequently the normalized Legendre polynomials satisfy
\[
 \|\phi_j\|_{\infty}=\sqrt{2j+1},
 \qquad
 -\frac{d}{du}\!\left((1-u^2)\frac{d\phi_j}{du}\right)
 =j(j+1)\phi_j,
 \qquad
 \|P_j'\|_\infty\le\frac{j(j+1)}2.
 \tag{2}
\]
Since \(A_j\ge j^2\) for \(j\ge1\),
\[
 \sum_{j\ge0}A_j^{-6}(2j+1)<\infty.
\]
Therefore the defining series gives
\[
 \sup_z k_{\mathrm{Leg}}(z,z)
 \le\left\{\sum_{j\ge0}A_j^{-6}(2j+1)\right\}^2<\infty.
 \tag{3}
\]
Moreover, \(|du/dz_1|\le1/2\), so (2) gives
\[
 \left\|\frac{d}{dz_1}\phi_j(\tanh(z_1/2))\right\|_{\infty}
 \le\frac{j(j+1)\sqrt{2j+1}}4.
\]
The squared derivative-section series is consequently bounded by a constant times \(\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-7}\), times the finite undifferentiated series in (3).  The same argument applies in the second coordinate.  The supremum norm of every tail is bounded by the corresponding tail of these convergent numerical series, so the series and their first derivatives converge uniformly and their limits are continuous and uniformly bounded.  This proves the first two defining bounds of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{src}}(K_{\mathrm{Leg}},C)\) for some finite constant.

It remains to prove, rather than assume, the source representation.  On the square \([-1,1]^2\), define
\[
 \mathscr D_uF=-\partial_u\{(1-u^2)\partial_uF\},
 \qquad
 \mathscr D_vF=-\partial_v\{(1-v^2)\partial_vF\}.
\]
The factors \(1-u^2\) and \(1-v^2\) eliminate every endpoint term in integration by parts.  Hence (2), orthogonality, and repeated integration by parts imply, for every smooth rational function \(F\) whose denominators are products of positive powers of \(1+au\), \(1+av\), and \(1+\varepsilon uv\),
\[
 \|F\|_{\mathcal H_{k_{\mathrm{Leg}}}}^2
 =\sum_{i,j\ge0}A_i^6A_j^6|\langle F,\psi_{ij}\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}|^2
 =\|(I+\mathscr D_u)^3(I+\mathscr D_v)^3F\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2.
 \tag{4}
\]
For completeness of this coefficient calculation on the functions used here, expand each reciprocal factor by its geometric series.  Since \(|au|,|av|,|\varepsilon uv|\le1/4\), the series and every fixed finite collection of differentiated series converge uniformly.  Their truncations are polynomials, and the Legendre polynomials span all polynomials by their nonzero leading coefficients.  Thus the relevant rational functions lie in the \(L^2(\mu)\)-closure of the tensor Legendre polynomials, which proves the last equality in (4) without an additional completeness hypothesis.

The Lebesgue score in environment \(e\) has the form
\[
 s_{\varepsilon,e}(z)=(-u,-v)^{\top}+\nabla_z\log w_{\varepsilon,e}(z).
 \tag{5}
\]
It is therefore a vector of smooth rational functions of \((u,v)\), with all denominators at least \(3/4\).  For each component \(s\) of (5), put
\[
 h=(I+\mathscr D_u)^6(I+\mathscr D_v)^6s,
 \qquad
 f=h/w_{\varepsilon,e}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Both \(h\) and \(f\) are of the type covered by (4), and hence belong to the scalar RKHS.  If \(s_{ij}=\langle s,\psi_{ij}\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}\), equations (2) and (6) give \(h_{ij}=A_i^6A_j^6s_{ij}\).  The integral operator of \(k_{\mathrm{Leg}}\) under \(\mu\) therefore satisfies
\[
 \langle L_{k_{\mathrm{Leg}},\mu}h,\psi_{ij}\rangle
 =A_i^{-6}A_j^{-6}h_{ij}=s_{ij}.
\]
The polynomial-closure argument following (4) yields \(L_{k_{\mathrm{Leg}},\mu}h=s\) in \(L^2(\mu)\), and continuity yields equality everywhere.  Since \(dP_{\varepsilon}^{[e]}=w_{\varepsilon,e}\,d\mu\),
\[
 L_{k_{\mathrm{Leg}},P_{\varepsilon}^{[e]}}f
 =L_{k_{\mathrm{Leg}},\mu}(w_{\varepsilon,e}f)
 =L_{k_{\mathrm{Leg}},\mu}h=s.
 \tag{7}
\]
Apply (6)--(7) componentwise to \(K_{\mathrm{Leg}}=k_{\mathrm{Leg}}I_2\).  Only finitely many derivatives occur.  Their suprema vary continuously over the compact parameter set \([0,1/4]\) and over three environments, while all denominators remain at least \(3/4\).  Equation (4) therefore bounds all source norms by one finite constant independent of \(\varepsilon\) and \(e\).  The scores in (5) are uniformly bounded, so they have a common finite exponential-moment bound.  Finally, every density is bounded by a constant times \(\ell(z_1)\ell(z_2)\), which decays exponentially at coordinate infinity; (3) and the derivative-section bounds then force all stated boundary products to zero.  Enlarging the common constant if needed proves
\(
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{log}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{src}}(K_{\mathrm{Leg}},C)
\).

For total variation, the observational densities at \(\varepsilon\) and zero differ by \(\varepsilon uv\) relative to \(\mu\), and the first-intervention densities differ by \(\varepsilon uv(1+au)\).  Symmetry gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_{\varepsilon}^{[0]},P_0^{[0]})
 =\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\mathbb E|UV|=\frac{\varepsilon}{8},
\]
and, because \(\mathbb E[U|U|]=0\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_{\varepsilon}^{[1]},P_0^{[1]})
 =\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\mathbb E[(1+aU)|UV|]
 =\frac{\varepsilon}{8}.
\]
The second-intervention law is independent of \(\varepsilon\).  The elementary product coupling bound
\(
\operatorname{TV}(\bigotimes_iQ_i,\bigotimes_iQ_i')
\le\sum_i\operatorname{TV}(Q_i,Q_i')
\)
follows by coupling each coordinate optimally and applying the union bound.  Applying it to \(N\) copies in each environment gives the claimed \(N\varepsilon/4\) bound and its limit.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(Q_0,Q_1,Q_2,\ldots\) be experiments on a fixed finite environment set \(\mathcal E\), each represented by independent infinite observation streams, and let \(\Gamma(Q)\) be its environment-labelled graph target.  Suppose \(\Gamma(Q_j)\ne\Gamma(Q_0)\) for every \(j\ge1\) and, for every finite \(N\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(
   \bigotimes_{m\in\mathcal E}Q_{j,m}^{\otimes N},
   \bigotimes_{m\in\mathcal E}Q_{0,m}^{\otimes N}
 \right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Let \(\mathsf D\) be any randomized sequential rule that may choose environments adaptively, stop at a data-dependent finite time, and return a singleton graph, a set of graphs, or abstention.  If its probability of any incorrect finite singleton return is uniformly at most \(\alpha\), namely
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\{Q_0,Q_1,Q_2,\ldots\}}
 \Pr_Q\!\left(
   \mathsf D\text{ makes a finite singleton return }\{\widehat\Gamma\}
   \text{ with }\widehat\Gamma\ne\Gamma(Q)
 \right)\le\alpha,
\]
then
\[
 \Pr_{Q_0}\!\left(
   \mathsf D\text{ ever makes the finite singleton return }\{\Gamma(Q_0)\}
 \right)\le\alpha.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Expose in advance the entire independent stream in every environment and an auxiliary random seed \(W\), independent of all streams and having the same law under every experiment.  Every adaptive sampling and randomization decision of \(\mathsf D\) is then a measurable function of these exposed objects; exposing unqueried observations changes neither the rule nor its distribution.

For \(N\ge1\), let \(E_N\) be the event that \(\mathsf D\) stops after inspecting at most \(N\) observations from each environment and returns the singleton \(\{\Gamma(Q_0)\}\).  The event \(E_N\) is measurable with respect to the first \(N\) observations of each full stream and \(W\).  Since \(\Gamma(Q_j)\ne\Gamma(Q_0)\), \(E_N\) is an incorrect finite singleton return under every \(Q_j\), and uniform validity gives
\[
 \Pr_{Q_j}(E_N)\le\alpha.
 \tag{8}
\]
Tensoring two laws with the same independent seed law does not increase total variation: for every event \(A\), integration of its seed sections gives
\[
 |(Q\otimes\mathcal L(W))(A)-(Q'\otimes\mathcal L(W))(A)|
 \le\operatorname{TV}(Q,Q').
\]
The assumed finite-prefix convergence therefore implies
\[
 |\Pr_{Q_j}(E_N)-\Pr_{Q_0}(E_N)|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Letting \(j\to\infty\) in (8) yields \(\Pr_{Q_0}(E_N)\le\alpha\) for every \(N\).

The events \(E_N\) increase with \(N\).  Any finite stopping history queries only finitely many observations in every member of the finite environment set, so
\[
 \bigcup_{N\ge1}E_N
 =\{\mathsf D\text{ ever makes the finite singleton return }\{\Gamma(Q_0)\}\}.
\]
Countable additivity, applied to the disjoint increments \(E_1,E_2\setminus E_1,\ldots\), gives continuity from below.  Hence
\[
 \Pr_{Q_0}\!\left(\bigcup_{N\ge1}E_N\right)
 =\lim_{N\to\infty}\Pr_{Q_0}(E_N)\le\alpha,
\]
which includes adaptive allocation, arbitrary independent randomization, and unbounded stopping times with finite realized return time.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let a model class contain the logistic null \(P_0^{\mathrm{log}}\) and \(P_{\varepsilon_j}^{\mathrm{log}}\) for some sequence \(\varepsilon_j\downarrow0\) with \(\varepsilon_j>0\).  Every randomized adaptive sequential procedure whose probability of any incorrect finite singleton environment-labelled graph return is uniformly at most \(\alpha\) on that class satisfies
\[
 \Pr_{P_0^{\mathrm{log}}}\!\left(
   \text{the procedure ever returns the correct singleton empty graph at a finite time}
 \right)\le\alpha.
\]
Consequently, a uniformly \(\alpha\)-valid procedure can have null correct-singleton return probability larger than \(\alpha\) only if its model class imposes some restriction excluding such graph-changing weak alternatives.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}logistic\mbox{-}boundary\mbox{-}legality}\), the graph target at \(P_0^{\mathrm{log}}\) is the empty graph, whereas every \(P_{\varepsilon_j}^{\mathrm{log}}\) has the arrow \(1\to2\).  Thus the targets differ.  The same proposition gives, for every fixed \(N\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(
   \bigotimes_{e=0}^2(P_{\varepsilon_j}^{[e]})^{\otimes N},
   \bigotimes_{e=0}^2(P_0^{[e]})^{\otimes N}
 \right)
 \le\frac{N\varepsilon_j}{4}\longrightarrow0.
\]
All hypotheses of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\mbox{-}prefix\mbox{-}continuity\mbox{-}no\mbox{-}return}\) hold with \(Q_0=P_0^{\mathrm{log}}\) and \(Q_j=P_{\varepsilon_j}^{\mathrm{log}}\).  That lemma gives the displayed probability bound.

For the final implication, take the contrapositive.  If a uniformly valid rule returns the null's correct singleton with probability greater than \(\alpha\), the class cannot contain a graph-changing sequence satisfying the displayed finite-prefix convergence.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}logistic\mbox{-}boundary\mbox{-}legality}\) proves that the present bounded-kernel source family is one explicit such sequence.  This logical necessity is exclusion of weak graph-changing alternatives; it neither singles out a numerical exclusion parameter nor supplies a rate comparison.

added_lemmas.statement:
At the logistic null \(P_0^{\mathrm{log}}\), the two singleton primitive score-correlation matrices are
\[
 R_1=\operatorname{diag}(c,0),\qquad
 R_2=\operatorname{diag}(0,c),
 \qquad
 c=\frac12\int_{-1}^1\frac{a^2(1-u^2)^2}{4(1+au)^2}\,du
 \ge\frac{2}{375}.
\]
All reached positive eigenvalues are therefore larger than \(g_0=1/375\), and the null's sole graph-loop projector comparison is one, hence is larger than \(h_0=1/2\).  For every \(0<\varepsilon\le1/4\), the alternative's reached singleton \(R_2\) is positive definite and
\[
 0<\lambda_{\min}(R_2)
 \le (R_2)_{11}
 \le\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4(1-\varepsilon)^2}
 \le\frac{4\varepsilon^2}{9}.
\]
Thus every \(0<\varepsilon<\min\{1/4,3\sqrt{g_0}/2\}\) has a reached positive eigenvalue in \((0,g_0)\).  The fixed public forbidden band includes the null but excludes all sufficiently small graph-changing alternatives used in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}no\mbox{-}return\mbox{-}logistic\mbox{-}null}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
At \(\varepsilon=0\), direct subtraction of the log densities in the definition gives, with \(u'=(1-u^2)/2\) and \(v'=(1-v^2)/2\),
\[
 d_1=\left(\frac{au'}{1+au},0\right)^{\!\top},
 \qquad
 d_2=\left(0,\frac{av'}{1+av}\right)^{\!\top}.
\]
Under the observational null, \(U,V\) are independent uniform variables.  Hence the primitive-correlation definition yields the two diagonal matrices in the statement, with the same positive entry \(c\).  Since \((1+aU)^2\le(1+a)^2\) and
\[
 \mathbb E(1-U^2)^2=1-\frac23+\frac15=\frac8{15},
\]
we obtain
\[
 c\ge\frac{a^2}{4(1+a)^2}\frac8{15}
 =\frac{2a^2}{15(1+a)^2}=\frac2{375}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Also \(R(\{1,2\})=cI_2\), so every nonzero eigenvalue of every null matrix occurrence is at least \(2/375>g_0\).  In the two-node order step both singleton deletions have rank one, and the public smallest-label rule removes label \(1\) first.  Substitution of the coordinate ranges into the only graph-loop test gives, up to the displayed ordering, the product \(P_{\operatorname{span}(e_2)}P_{\operatorname{span}(e_2)}\), whose operator norm is one.  Thus the projector band with \(h_0=1/2\) also holds.

For \(\varepsilon>0\), subtraction of the observational score from the second-intervention score gives
\[
 d_2(u,v)=
 \left(
 -\frac{\varepsilon u'v}{1+\varepsilon uv},
 \frac{av'}{1+av}-\frac{\varepsilon uv'}{1+\varepsilon uv}
 \right)^{\!\top}.
 \tag{10}
\]
To prove positive definiteness, suppose \(x d_{2,1}+y d_{2,2}=0\) almost surely.  Positivity of the observational density and continuity make the equality valid throughout \((-1,1)^2\).  At \(v=0\), the first component vanishes and the second is \((a-\varepsilon u)/2>0\), so \(y=0\).  At \(u=0\) and \(v\ne0\), the first component is \(-\varepsilon v/2\ne0\), so \(x=0\).  Therefore every nonzero vector \(q\) has
\(
q^{\top}R_2q=\mathbb E[(q^{\top}d_2)^2]>0
\), proving that \(R_2\) is positive definite.

Rayleigh's principle and the first component of (10) give
\[
 0<\lambda_{\min}(R_2)
 \le e_1^{\top}R_2e_1
 =\mathbb E_{P_{\varepsilon}^{[0]}}\!\left[
   \frac{\varepsilon^2u'^2v^2}{(1+\varepsilon uv)^2}
 \right]
 \le\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4(1-\varepsilon)^2}.
\]
For \(\varepsilon\le1/4\), the last quantity is at most \(4\varepsilon^2/9\).  Every singleton is an encoder query in \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\), so this eigenvalue is reached regardless of order ties.  If \(0<\varepsilon<3\sqrt{g_0}/2\), then \(4\varepsilon^2/9<g_0\).  Hence the alternative violates \(\{0\}\cup[g_0,\infty)\), whereas (9) and the projector calculation show that the null satisfies both fixed public bands.

proposed.name: bounded-kernel logistic boundary family
proposed.construction:
Let \(\ell(z)=e^{-z}/(1+e^{-z})^2\) be the standard logistic density, put \(a=1/4\), and, for \(z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb R^2\), put \(u=\tanh(z_1/2)\), \(v=\tanh(z_2/2)\), and \(\mu(dz)=\ell(z_1)\ell(z_2)\,dz_1dz_2\).  For \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/4\), define the three-environment experiment \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{log}}=(P_{\varepsilon}^{[e]}:e\in\{0,1,2\})\) by the densities, relative to \(\mu\),
\[
 w_{\varepsilon,0}=1+\varepsilon uv,\qquad
 w_{\varepsilon,1}=(1+au)(1+\varepsilon uv),\qquad
 w_{\varepsilon,2}=1+av.
\]
Equivalently, the observational root density is \(\ell(z_1)\), its second-node conditional density is \(\ell(z_2)(1+\varepsilon uv)\), intervention \(1\) replaces only the root density by \(\ell(z_1)(1+au)\), and intervention \(2\) replaces only the second-node conditional by \(\ell(z_2)(1+av)\).  The intervention-target map is the identity.  Let \(\mathcal G_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{log}}\) be the empty DAG when \(\varepsilon=0\) and the DAG with the single arrow \(1\to2\) when \(\varepsilon>0\), and set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{log}}=\{P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{log}}:0\le\varepsilon\le1/4\}\).

For the common source class, let \(\phi_j=\sqrt{2j+1}\,P_j\), where \(P_j\) is the degree-\(j\) Legendre polynomial, and put \(A_j=1+j(j+1)\), \(\psi_{ij}(z)=\phi_i(u)\phi_j(v)\), and
\[
 k_{\mathrm{Leg}}(z,z')=

\[

proposed_core_edits.reason: The active directive requires the explicit normalized logistic null, its legal graph-changing alternatives, and their common Legendre source class as one declared construction.

prose_updates.tldr: As an exact-real statistical procedure on the declared linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset class, the certificate returns the environment-labelled transitive closure \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and an environment-indexed encoder estimate within \(\tau\) of the parent-supported population range class, or abstains. Its per-environment sample dependence is quadratic in \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear in \(\log(1/\alpha)\), up to the displayed logarithms, and rational post-summary decisions have a proved polynomial-bit realization. The encoder output is neither asserted invertible nor a unique representative of a repeated positive eigenspace. A separate explicit bounded-kernel logistic family gives the intrinsic boundary: if a model class contains graph-changing alternatives converging to its empty-graph null in every finite-prefix total variation, every uniformly \(\alpha\)-valid randomized sequential rule returns the correct singleton empty graph there with probability at most \(\alpha\). Thus some restriction excluding such weak alternatives is necessary for high-probability finite singleton certification, while public reached gaps are one sufficient restriction on the Gaussian class; the theorem does not make the particular \(g_0,h_0\) parameters necessary, establish a minimax rate, or show failure of a named published workflow. Separately, a legal all-dimension Gaussian family has constant reached gaps but a positive unqueried equation-(22) margin that vanishes exponentially, proving no positive dimension-uniform constant lower bound on that margin is necessary and that the corresponding sufficient sample analysis is exponentially pessimistic on this family without contradicting its existential premise.

project_justification.gap: Finite singleton graph certification is not uniformly reliable at a graph-changing boundary merely because each fixed model is identifiable: a sequence of legal weak alternatives may converge to an empty-graph null on every finite data prefix. Separately, Acartürk et al.'s finite-sample analysis pays for equation (22)'s all-subset positive-eigenvalue minimum although the deterministic recovery program executes only a polynomial transcript, and its printed equation-(23) norm product is not the reciprocal lower bound supplied by actual projector geometry.
project_justification.niche: The note pairs a public query-local sufficient contract for an exact-real Gaussian recover-or-abstain certificate with an intrinsic finite-return boundary showing that some model restriction must exclude graph-changing weak alternatives. The boundary concerns uniform decision validity, not comparative failure of any named algorithm.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the Gaussian certificate with public reached gaps, the cap \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}<66q_{\star}u_{\star}\), environment-labelled graph and parent-range encoder targets, explicit error bars, and polynomial-bit post-summary realization. It also supplies an explicit common-kernel logistic family, proves its intervention and source legality by a Legendre differential-operator construction, derives finite-prefix total-variation convergence, and proves the exact \(\alpha\) null singleton-return ceiling for every uniformly valid randomized adaptive sequential rule on a class containing those alternatives. This necessity statement is only the need for some exclusion; it does not privilege \(g_0,h_0\), give a minimax rate, or criticize a named workflow. The positive theorem remains confined to the Gaussian variance-reset subclass. Over the broader published class, the Gaussian witness establishes only the absence of a necessary positive dimension-uniform constant equation-(22) margin and exponential pessimism of that sufficient analysis, while preserving the source theorem's model-specific existential threshold premise.

prose_updates.interpretation: The positive and negative theorems address different quantifiers. On the publicly promised Gaussian class, fixed reached bands make every rank and projector decision stable and yield high-probability finite graph and encoder certification. At the logistic null, uniform validity over arbitrarily weak graph-changing alternatives forces the probability of a finite correct singleton return down to at most \(\alpha\); set output, abstention, or delayed return remain available. The forbidden-band proposition connects the two sides by showing that the fixed public Gaussian-style band contains the null but excludes the very alternatives that drive the continuity argument. This certifies one sufficient design and one general exclusion requirement, not necessity of the numerical \(g_0,h_0\) formulation, a minimax phase rate, or failure of any published method.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The numerical theorem is post-summary: it assumes outward rational enclosures of exact fixed-coordinate empirical covariance summaries and, when an ambient encoder is requested, an enclosure of the canonical support frame. Raw-data processing additionally incurs representation, reading, and covariance-formation cost, including at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) record operations. The statistical theorem remains exact-real at the sampling layer, and the encoder guarantee is distance to a unit-row parent-supported range class, not invertibility or a unique repeated-eigenspace representative. The positive guarantee is specific to Gaussian variance resets. The logistic converse controls only finite correct singleton graph returns under uniform error validity; it does not forbid honest set output, abstention, pointwise procedures, or guarantees on classes that exclude the graph-changing sequence.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The positive statistical and polynomial-bit post-summary theorems concern the linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset subclass in fixed coordinates on \(\mathcal S\), target only \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and the environment-indexed parent-supported encoder range, and do not transfer upward to the full smooth soft-intervention class. Public reached gaps \(g_0,h_0\) are sufficient for this certificate and are a pre-sampling promise, never inferred from realized empirical gaps. The logistic theorem proves a more general necessity statement only in form: a class supporting high-probability finite singleton certification at that null must exclude the exhibited graph-changing finite-prefix approximants by some restriction. It does not prove that these particular gap parameters are necessary, determine any minimax rate, or establish failure of Acartürk et al., Lee--Jin--Aragam, or any other named workflow. The rational algorithm is polynomial only after covariance summaries are supplied; raw records still cost at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) to read. The Gaussian separation family has positive all-subset margin at every fixed dimension and therefore proves only that no positive dimension-uniform constant equation-(22) lower bound is necessary and that the equation-(22)-controlled sufficient sample bound is exponentially pessimistic relative to constant reached gaps. Actual projector geometry and \(\rho_i(G)\) replace the false printed norm-product identity. Neither an invertible encoder nor a canonical representative of a repeated positive eigenspace is claimed.
